Health, stamina, and spirit stat commit candidate

Corrected character-manager global slot (RVA 0x6C29C68, not the dead 0x6C29C88 accessor candidate). Found by converting a working third-party TU 2.01.00 build's live-logged addresses to RVAs; this is one of ~50 call sites that read `manager = *(*0x6C29C68)` and pass it as arg1 (RCX) to a shared char-manager API helper (0x1429b39d0 in the analyzed image). Anchored on the ABI-fixed dereference-into-arg1 step plus two literal offsets (RBP+0xDC, RSP+0x40) from one specific call site, not the allocator-chosen registers around it.
Corrected character-manager global slot (RVA 0x6C29C68), second independent call site for cross-checking Candidate_A - a different function, same shared API helper (0x1429b39d0).

Pathing helper (destination-following movement override) candidate. Found by converting a working third-party TU 2.01.00 build's live-logged hook address (RVA 0x35C8000) to a function entry, then diffing its prologue against the dead TU 2.00.00 kSig_PathingHelper: the compiler switched from an RSP-relative shadow-space prologue (`48 89 5C 24 08...`) to an RAX-copy-of-RSP prologue (`48 8B C4 48 89 58 08...`), but everything from the R14/RSI register setup onward (`4D 8B F0 48 8B F2 66 C7 45 ?? 04 00 C6 45 ?? 01 33 DB 48 89 5D ?? 48 89 5D ??`) is byte-identical to the old signature's tail. Pattern starts at the function's true entry point (verified: Ghidra reports ENTRY=0x1435c8000 for this exact match).

signatures.feature: World master frame update (Game Speed / Timescale) candidate. Found the same way as the pathing-helper: a working third-party build's live-logged hook address (RVA 0xA541C0) diffed against the dead TU 2.00.00 kSig_MasterFrameUpdate. The register-save prologue changed shape (one extra PUSH R12, RSI saved via push instead of a shadow-space store, different stack/XMM-save offsets), but the semantic body starting at `48 8B F9 48 8B 51 60 8B 42 64 89 42 60` (RDI=RCX; RDX=[RCX+0x60] i.e. TimeManager; EAX=[RDX+0x64]; [RDX+0x60]=EAX) is byte-identical and matches the documented TimeManager access exactly. Pattern starts at the true function entry (Ghidra: ENTRY=0x140a541c0, 1 caller).

signatures.feature: Durable dye-record upsert candidate. The old kSig_DyeUpsert/_1180 patterns anchor mid-function (this build's compiled function needs a full register-save prologue where the old one apparently did not, so those bytes no longer exist at all on this build). Found the true function entry from a working third-party build's live-logged address (RVA 0x2353FE0, `dye: durable upsert @ ...`) via Ghidra (ENTRY=0x142353fe0). The body from the prologue through the documented 16-byte record-stride shift (`49 C1 E0 04`, same literal the old signature's own comment already called out as semantic) is fully literal, no wildcards needed - this build's stack offsets happen to match byte-for-byte at this exact point.
signatures.source: COMPATIBILITY.md: BREAKTHROUGH (2026-09-08) - teleport/world/dye signatures re-derived via gugi97 v0.19.0 cross-reference

signatures.feature: Parry verdict site candidate. The compiler swapped the VCOMISS operand order on this build (`VCOMISS XMM2,XMM3` -> `VCOMISS XMM3,XMM2`), changing only the ModRM byte (`D3` -> `DA`); the SETA + store that immediately follow (the actual patch site, `kSetaOffset=4` bytes into the match per parry.cpp) are byte-identical. Confirmed via a working third-party build's live-logged address (RVA 0x7FC528, `parry: verdict site @ ...`): Ghidra shows `0F 97 C0` (SETA AL) starting at exactly that RVA, 4 bytes after this pattern's start - matching parry.cpp's own kSetaOffset exactly.
signatures.source: COMPATIBILITY.md: BREAKTHROUGH (2026-09-08) - teleport/world/dye/parry signatures re-derived via gugi97 v0.19.0 cross-reference

signatures.feature: Locomotion sub-step driver (Super Run) candidate. Not found via a third-party log address (gugi97's v0.19.0 build reorganizes its own logging for this feature - its 'airborne mover' log line does not exist anywhere in this project's own source, so an absent error line there proves nothing). Instead found by walking a known-good anchor: kAirMover_Lo/Hi (teleport.cpp, RVA range 0x35C3290-0x35C3C5C, itself live-identified via the third-party log) is the airborne mover's own function; Ghidra's decompile of that function (ENTRY=0x1435c3290) calls FUN_1435be940 three times with the exact hkLocoStep argument shape (comp, *dt-by-value, &vel-stack-buffer, 0, ptr, 0, 0). That callee's prologue keeps the old signature's distinctive byte-parameter store (`44 88 48 20`) byte-identical, with one extra qword home-store inserted before the pushes shifting the frame literals by a consistent 0x10 (0x798->0x788, 0x860->0x850). It also calls the already-independently-confirmed kSig_MoveUpdate (RVA 0x418EFC0, unchanged on this build) and has 12 callers, consistent with a stepper shared across movement modes.
signatures.source: COMPATIBILITY.md: BREAKTHROUGH (2026-09-08/09) - LocoStepper re-derived by walking the airborne-mover anchor to its callee

signatures.feature: Inventory item-quantity accessor candidate (the FATAL signature Inventory::Install() checks first). Found via a Cheat Engine table the user supplied, built specifically against this exact build (1.0.0.2760, 'Crimson Desert Ultimate Table.CT' v5.0) - its own AOB for the bucket-capacity check (`CMP [rax+0x10],0; JLE; CMP byte[rax+0xA0],0`) matched offline at RVA 0x20819AD inside a small function (Ghidra ENTRY=0x142081950) whose prologue register-saves (`MOV RDI,R8; MOVZX EBX,DX; MOV RSI,RCX`) match this project's own already-declared 3-argument GetItemQty_t signature (container, uint16_t typeId, void* keyPtr) field-for-field - the old dead pattern's tail (`49 8B E8 0F B7 DA`) is the same MOVZX plus a save of the same R8 argument, just to a different register (RBP there, RDI here).
signatures.source: COMPATIBILITY.md: Inventory re-derived via a user-supplied build-matched Cheat Engine table (2026-09-10)

signatures.feature: Durable inventory container-registry global anchor candidate. The same user-supplied, build-matched Cheat Engine table documents this exact problem in its own commentary: '2.01.00 RECOMPILED THE HEAD OF THIS SEQUENCE, and that is the whole of the container editor was not found in this build' - the chain TAIL (+0x30/+0x50, matching this project's own kOff_Global_Mid/kOff_Mid_Container) is unchanged; only the head changed from `mov rax, cs:<global>; mov rdx,[rax+30h]` to `lea rdx,[rsp+?]; mov rcx, cs:<global>; mov rcx,[rcx+30h]`. Verified via Ghidra against this exact build: the RIP load resolves to RVA 0x6C29760, matching the CT table's own independently-reported value exactly.
